teams.heading: Fiji secure Pacific Nations Cup final place after defeating Canada in Osaka
teams.body: Fiji have secured their place in the Pacific Nations Cup final after defeating Canada in Friday’s semi-final in Osaka. Playing without several European-based stars, the defending champions maintained the attacking flair Canada coach Stephen Meehan expected, noting that "Fiji is going to have all the physical attributes and will be throwing the ball around in all sorts of fashions." While the squad prepares for the final, the community is mourning the death of Saimoni Vunilagi, who died Friday in Fukuoka following a suspected training-ground heatstroke.

lead.why: Fiji winning their semi-final to reach the Pacific Nations Cup final is the primary competitive milestone for the national team in today's coverage.

teams.heading: RFU extends Steve Borthwick's contract to avoid World Cup uncertainty
teams.body: The Rugby Football Union has extended Steve Borthwick’s contract until the conclusion of the 2028 Six Nations, a move designed to remove coaching speculation ahead of next year's World Cup. While the extension provides stability, performance director Conor O’Shea clarified that Borthwick’s long-term future remains dependent on results in Australia. “You don’t want them looking for a job going into a World Cup,” O’Shea explained, while insisting he believes this England team is capable of winning the tournament.

teams.heading: IRFU rules out moving any Ireland Six Nations matches to USA
teams.body: The IRFU has confirmed there are "currently no plans or discussions" regarding Ireland playing Six Nations fixtures in the United States. While World Rugby chief executive Alan Gilpin recently suggested that moving matches to American markets could help expand the sport, the governing body reiterated that the tournament holds a unique place for supporters. The union emphasised that the ability for fans to watch their teams on home soil remains a central and non-negotiable part of the competition's appeal.

teams.heading: Gonzalo Quesada remains suspended for upcoming Italy match against South Africa
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada will be absent from the stadium for the forthcoming meeting with South Africa. Quesada is currently serving a two-Test suspension, the first issued under World Rugby’s new Match Official Abuse Sanctioning Process. The independent judicial panel implemented the ban following critical remarks made regarding the officiating during Italy's match against the All Blacks in July. As per the regulations, the coach is prohibited from all match-day proceedings until the completion of his suspension.

lead.why: The report confirms Gonzalo Quesada's two-Test suspension remains in effect for the upcoming fixture against South Africa.

teams.heading: Rhea Clarke and Evie Gallagher start for Scotland against Canada today
teams.body: Scotland begin their WXV Series campaign today with Rhea Clarke earning her first start at scrum-half. Interim head coach Dave Butcher has also included Evie Gallagher at openside flanker, marking her first appearance since last year’s World Cup. Helen Nelson confirmed the squad has moved on from the recent coaching transition, focusing on the test against a Canadian side that defeated Scotland 40-19 during their last meeting at the World Cup.

teams.heading: New technical director Rhys Long outlines vision for Wales’s future
teams.body: Rhys Long has reaffirmed his commitment to transforming Welsh rugby’s long-term talent development, moving away from cyclical performance patterns. Having returned to the WRU in a senior role reporting to Dave Reddin, Long aims to implement a system designed for a 10 to 15-year horizon rather than short-term gains. “I wouldn’t have taken this job if I didn’t think we could put in place the talent development system that I know we’re capable of,” Long stated earlier this week.

lead.why: The new technical director has publicly committed to a long-term talent pathway overhaul to address the current performance gap.

teams.heading: Argentina reflect on mixed results during challenging five-match international window
teams.body: Argentina enter the next phase of the international season having endured a testing run in their last five matches. During this period, the Pumas recorded one victory, three defeats, and one draw. The most recent of these fixtures saw the side secure a 28-28 stalemate against Australia on home soil earlier this month. As the squad prepares for the upcoming November programme, the focus remains on improving consistency following a series that highlighted both resilient defensive efforts and execution challenges.

teams.heading: James Slipper pauses playing career for new Brumbies scrum coaching role
teams.body: Veteran Wallabies prop James Slipper has been appointed as the Brumbies' new scrum coach on a temporary basis. The 154-Test international, who remains under contract with the club for another season, will step away from on-field duties during Super Rugby AUS to focus on mentoring the next generation of forwards. Slipper, who replaces John Ulugia after his departure to the Wallabies' staff, noted: “I’m not trying to reinvent the wheel. I’m just trying to give them some things that I’ve learnt.”

teams.heading: Eddie Jones Targets Cup Glory As Japan Faces USA In Osaka
teams.body: Japan opens its Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup campaign today in the semifinal against the USA Eagles at Hanazono Rugby Stadium. Head Coach Eddie Jones will be targeting cup glory at home after two consecutive years of finishing behind Fiji in the tournament. Japan enters the match as favourites, currently ranked 12th compared to the USA's 14th. While the historical head-to-head is tight, Japan has won nine of the last ten encounters, including the previous four matchups.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie names Richie Mo’unga in reshuffled side for Baltimore finale
teams.body: Coach Dave Rennie has finalised a revamped lineup for the series conclusion, handing Richie Mo’unga a start at flyhalf. With the All Blacks trailing 2-1, the selection also sees Josh Moorby return to the wing and Anton Lienert-Brown feature at outside centre. Springbok assistant coach Mzwandile Stick acknowledged the threat, noting, “We know Richie Mo’unga is world-class. As the coaching staff, we expected that selection,” and warned that the visitors are expected to be “even more bold” in their attacking approach.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus keeps faith as Springboks chase series victory in Baltimore
teams.body: South Africa head into the final Test of the series in Baltimore holding a 2-1 lead and looking to secure the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry trophy outright. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has made minimal changes to his squad, with Damian Willemse replacing the injured Cheslin Kolbe at full-back and Morne van den Berg taking over at scrum-half. The world champions remain focused on maintaining their forward dominance after recent victories in Cape Town and Soweto solidified their position at the top.
